reason: This text from 2 Samuel 13 narrates the rape of Tamar by her half-brother Amnon, a prince of Israel. The passage depicts a grave injustice perpetrated within the royal household and shows King David's failure to execute proper justice—he becomes angry but does not adequately address or punish the crime. The narrative illustrates the breakdown and failure of governmental authority to protect the vulnerable and maintain justice, leading to bitter resentment and eventual violent consequences (Absalom's later revenge). The text does not present or model good leadership or functioning government to the people's benefit; rather, it demonstrates the opposite—the harmful consequences when leadership fails to properly address grave injustice.
